      "text": "# [[Rotational Dynamics and Mechanics]]\n\nThis file consolidates lecture notes covering rotational dynamics, conservation of angular momentum, collisions, and work-energy theorems on inclined planes. The material progresses from variable mass systems to rigid body collisions and energy conservation.\n\n---\n\n## 1. [[General Formulas and Identities]]\n\n### Rotational Mechanics\n*   **Angular Momentum ($\\Gamma$ or $L$):**\n    $$ \\Gamma \u003d J \\cdot \\omega $$\n    Where $J$ is the moment of inertia and $\\omega$ is angular velocity.\n*   **Conservation of Angular Momentum:**\n    $$ \\Gamma_{initial} \u003d \\Gamma_{final} \\implies J_1 \\omega_1 \u003d J_2 \\omega_2 $$\n    *Valid when the sum of external torques is zero ($\\sum M \u003d 0$).*\n*   **Steiner’s Theorem (Parallel Axis Theorem):**\n    $$ J \u003d J_{cm} + m d^2 $$\n    Where $J_{cm}$ is the moment of inertia around the center of mass, and $d$ is the distance to the new parallel axis.\n*   **Rotational Kinetic Energy:**\n    $$ W_{rot} \u003d \\frac{1}{2} J \\omega^2 $$\n\n### Work and Energy\n*   **Work ($A$):**\n    $$ A \u003d \\int \\vec{F} \\cdot d\\vec{r} $$\n*   **Kinetic Energy (Translational):**\n    $$ W_{kin} \u003d \\frac{1}{2} m v^2 $$\n\n---\n\n## 2. Problem Solving and Analysis\n\n### 2.1. [[Variable Moment of Inertia]]: The Salt Spreader\n**Context:** A rotating disk (salt spreader) is spinning. Salt falling onto or off the disk changes the total mass distribution over time, affecting the angular velocity due to conservation of angular momentum.\n\n#### Derivation logic:\n1.  **System:** A plate (disk) and salt.\n2.  **Assumption:** No external torque ($\\Gamma_0 \u003d \\text{const}$).\n3.  **Variable:** Mass of salt changes linearly with time $m_{salt} \\propto t$ (or mass flow $\\Phi_m$).\n\n**Step 1: Define Moment of Inertia ($J$)**\n$$ J(t) \u003d J_{plate} + J_{salt}(t) $$\n$$ J_{plate} \u003d \\frac{1}{2} M R^2 $$\nIf salt acts as a uniform layer or point mass at radius $b$:\n$$ J_{salt}(t) \u003d (\\Phi_m \\cdot t) \\cdot b^2 $$\n*Note: $\\Phi_m$ is the mass flow rate (kg/s).*\n\n**Step 2: Angular Velocity as a function of time**\nUsing conservation $\\Gamma_0 \u003d J(t) \\omega(t)$:\n$$ \\omega(t) \u003d \\frac{\\Gamma_0}{J_{plate} + \\Phi_m b^2 t} $$\nThis can be simplified to the form:\n$$ \\omega(t) \u003d \\omega_0 \\frac{A}{B + t} $$\nWhere $A$ and $B$ represent the constant inertia terms.\n\n**Step 3: Calculating Angle of Rotation ($\\phi$)**\nTo find the total angle turned, we integrate angular velocity:\n$$ \\phi(t) \u003d \\int_0^t \\omega(t\u0027) dt\u0027 \u003d \\int_0^t \\frac{C}{D + t\u0027} dt\u0027 $$\n**Integration Recall:** $\\int \\frac{1}{x} dx \u003d \\ln|x|$.\n$$ \\phi(t) \u003d C \\left[ \\ln(D + t\u0027) \\right]_0^t \u003d C \\ln\\left(\\frac{D+t}{D}\\right) $$\n\n\u003e **Critical Analysis:** The lecturer emphasizes that while $\\omega$ decreases as mass is added (or changes), the total angle $\\phi$ grows logarithmically. This is a classic \"rocket equation\" style integration but applied to rotation.\n\n---\n\n### 2.2. [[Inelastic Collisions]]: Rod and Dart (Pikado)\n**Context:** A wooden rod of mass $m_{rod}$ and length $d$ hangs or pivots. A dart (pikado) of mass $m$ hits it with velocity $v$.\n\n#### Scenario A: Dart hits a hanging rod\n1.  **Conservation of Angular Momentum:** The linear momentum of the dart is converted into angular momentum of the system relative to the pivot.\n    $$ \\Gamma_{dart} \u003d \\vec{r} \\times \\vec{p} \u003d d \\cdot (m v) $$\n2.  **System Moment of Inertia (After Impact):**\n    $$ J_{total} \u003d J_{rod} + J_{dart} $$\n    *   $J_{rod}$ around pivot (using Steiner if pivot is at end): $J_{rod} \u003d \\frac{1}{3} m_{rod} d^2$.\n    *   $J_{dart} \u003d m_{dart} d^2$ (treated as point mass at distance $d$).\n3.  **Resulting Angular Velocity:**\n    $$ \\omega \u003d \\frac{\\Gamma_{dart}}{J_{total}} $$\n\n#### Scenario B: Energy Loss ($\\Delta W$)\nThe collision is plastic (inelastic). Energy is **not** conserved.\n$$ \\Delta W \u003d W_{final} - W_{initial} \u003d \\frac{1}{2} J_{total} \\omega^2 - \\frac{1}{2} m_{dart} v^2 $$\n\u003e **Warning:** A common student error is to try to conserve Energy during the impact. **Do not do this.** Only Angular Momentum is conserved during the impact forces. Energy is lost to deformation/heat.\n\n---\n\n### 2.3. [[Rotational Energy]]: The Acrobat/Skier\n**Context:** An acrobat or skier changes their body shape mid-flight (tucking in arms/legs).\n*   **Initial state:** Large moment of inertia $J_1$, slow rotation $\\omega_1$.\n*   **Final state:** Small moment of inertia $J_2$, fast rotation $\\omega_2$.\n\n**Calculations:**\n1.  **Conservation:** $J_1 \\omega_1 \u003d J_2 \\omega_2 \\implies \\omega_2 \u003d \\omega_1 \\frac{J_1}{J_2}$.\n2.  **Work Done by Acrobat:** The acrobat must perform work to pull their mass inward against centrifugal force. This manifests as an increase in kinetic energy.\n    $$ \\Delta W_{kin} \u003d \\frac{1}{2} J_2 \\omega_2^2 - \\frac{1}{2} J_1 \\omega_1^2 $$\n    Since $J_1 \u003e J_2$ and angular momentum is constant, $W_{kin}$ actually **increases**.\n\n---\n\n### 2.4. [[Dynamics]]: Block on an Inclined Plane\n**Context:** A block of mass $m\u003d50kg$ is pushed/pulled up a slope ($d\u003d6m$, $\\alpha\u003d30^\\circ$) with constant velocity. Friction coefficient $k_{tr}\u003d0.2$.\n\n**Objective:** Calculate the force $F$ required and the Work done ($A$).\n\n**Force Decomposition:**\nThe force $F$ acts at an angle $\\alpha$ relative to the slope (horizontal push on a wedge geometry).\n1.  **Axes:**\n    *   $x$: Parallel to slope.\n    *   $y$: Perpendicular to slope.\n2.  **Forces in $y$ (Perpendicular):**\n    $$ F_N - F_g \\cos\\alpha - F \\sin\\alpha \u003d 0 $$\n    $$ F_N \u003d mg \\cos\\alpha + F \\sin\\alpha $$\n    *Note: The pushing force $F$ adds to the normal force because it has a component pushing into the slope.*\n3.  **Forces in $x$ (Parallel, moving up):**\n    $$ F \\cos\\alpha - F_g \\sin\\alpha - F_{tr} \u003d 0 $$\n    Where Friction $F_{tr} \u003d k_{tr} F_N$.\n\n**Solving for F:**\nSubstitute $F_N$ into the $x$-equation:\n$$ F \\cos\\alpha - mg \\sin\\alpha - k_{tr}(mg \\cos\\alpha + F \\sin\\alpha) \u003d 0 $$\nGroup terms with $F$:\n$$ F (\\cos\\alpha - k_{tr} \\sin\\alpha) \u003d mg (\\sin\\alpha + k_{tr} \\cos\\alpha) $$\n$$ F \u003d mg \\frac{\\sin\\alpha + k_{tr} \\cos\\alpha}{\\cos\\alpha - k_{tr} \\sin\\alpha} $$\n\n**Calculating Work ($A$):**\n$$ A \u003d \\int \\vec{F} \\cdot d\\vec{r} $$\nSince force is constant and parallel to displacement component:\n$$ A \u003d (F \\cos\\alpha) \\cdot d $$\n*(Alternatively, calculate total work done against gravity and friction).*\n\n\u003e **Critical Analysis:** The formula for $F$ reveals a singularity. If $\\cos\\alpha - k_{tr} \\sin\\alpha \u003d 0$, the force required becomes infinite. This corresponds to the condition of \"self-locking\" where pushing harder just increases friction more than it helps move the block.\n\n---\n\n## 3. [[Work and Energy]]: Bungee/Spring Problem\n**Context:** Mass $m$ falls from height $h$, attached to a spring/rope with stiffness $k$. Find max extension $x$.\n\n**Conservation of Energy:**\n$$ W_{initial} \u003d W_{final} + W_{losses} $$\n1.  **Initial:** Potential Energy $W_p \u003d m g (h+x)$. (Assuming reference level at bottom).\n    *   *Correction in notes:* Often reference is at equilibrium or start. Let\u0027s look at the notes: $W_{kin} + W_p + W_{elas} \u003d const$.\n2.  **State 1 (Top):** $v\u003d0$, extension\u003d0. Energy \u003d $m g h$.\n3.  **State 2 (Bottom):** $v\u003d0$, extension\u003d$x$. Energy \u003d $\\frac{1}{2} k x^2$.\n4.  **Work by Friction/Drag ($W_{pr}$):** If friction is present, $m g h \u003d \\frac{1}{2} k x^2 + W_{pr}$.\n\n**Equation:**\n$$ m g (h+d) - \\frac{1}{2} k d^2 \u003d 0 $$\nThis forms a quadratic equation for $d$ (distance stretched).\n$$ d \u003d \\frac{-b \\pm \\sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} $$\n\n---\n\n## 4. Notable Memorializations\n*   **The \"Pikado\" (Dart) example:** The lecturer uses a specific scenario of a dart hitting a rod to illustrate angular momentum conservation versus energy loss.\n*   **\"Graceful\" Derivation:** The instructor jokingly referred to the messy board derivation of the variable mass problem as \"graciozno\" (graceful/elegant) despite the complexity.\n*   **The Logarithm:** Special emphasis was placed on the fact that while rotational speed drops with mass addition, the total angle leads to a logarithmic term ($\\ln(t)$).\n\n---\n\n## 5. [[Warning]] / Common Pitfalls\n1.  **Steiner\u0027s Theorem:** Do not forget to shift the moment of inertia if the rotation axis is not the center of mass.\n    *   *Correct:* $J \u003d J_{cm} + md^2$.\n    *   *Incorrect:* $J \u003d J_{cm}$.\n2.  **Normal Force on Incline:** When an external force $F$ pushes on a block at an angle, $F_N$ is **not** just $mg \\cos\\alpha$. You must account for the component of $F$ pressing into the surface ($F \\sin\\alpha$). This increases friction.\n3.  **Conservation Confusion:**\n    *   **Collision:** Conserve **Momentum/Angular Momentum**. Energy is usually lost.\n    *   **Movement (Springs/Gravity):** Conserve **Energy**. Momentum changes due to external forces (gravity/spring mount).",

        "text": "$ or $L$):**\n    $$ \\Gamma \u003d J \\cdot \\omega $$\n    Where $J"
      }, {
        "text": "$ is the moment of inertia and $\\omega$ is angular velocity.\n*   **Conservation of Angular Momentum:**\n    $$ \\"
      }, {
        "text": "Gamma_{initial} \u003d \\Gamma_{final} \\implies J_1 \\omega_1 \u003d J_2 \\omega_2"
      }, {
        "text": " $$\n    *Valid when the sum of external torques is zero ($\\sum M \u003d 0$).*\n*   **"
      }, {
        "text": "Steiner’s Theorem (Parallel Axis Theorem):**\n    $$ J \u003d J_{cm} + m d^2 $$\n    Where $J"
      }, {
        "text": "_{cm}$ is the moment of inertia around the center of mass, and $d$ is the distance to the new parallel"
      }, {
        "text": " axis.\n*   **Rotational Kinetic Energy:**\n    $$ W_{rot} \u003d \\frac{1}{"
      }, {
        "text": "2} J \\omega^2 $$\n\n### Work and Energy\n*   **Work ($A$):**\n    $$ A"
      }, {
        "text": " \u003d \\int \\vec{F} \\cdot d\\vec{r} $$\n*   **Kinetic Energy ("
      }, {
        "text": "Translational):**\n    $$ W_{kin} \u003d \\frac{1}{2} m v^2 $$\n\n"
      }, {
        "text": "---\n\n## 2. Problem Solving and Analysis\n\n### 2.1. [[Variable Moment of Inertia]]: The Salt Spreader"
      }, {
        "text": "\n**Context:** A rotating disk (salt spreader) is spinning. Salt falling onto or off the disk changes the total mass distribution"
      }, {
        "text": " over time, affecting the angular velocity due to conservation of angular momentum.\n\n#### Derivation logic:\n1.  **System"
      }, {
        "text": ":** A plate (disk) and salt.\n2.  **Assumption:** No external torque ($\\Gamma_0 \u003d \\text{const}$)."
      }, {
        "text": "\n3.  **Variable:** Mass of salt changes linearly with time $m_{salt} \\propto t$ (or mass"
      }, {
        "text": " flow $\\Phi_m$).\n\n**Step 1: Define Moment of Inertia ($J$)**\n$$ J(t) \u003d"
      }, {
        "text": " J_{plate} + J_{salt}(t) $$\n$$ J_{plate} \u003d \\frac{1}{"
      }, {
        "text": "2} M R^2 $$\nIf salt acts as a uniform layer or point mass at radius $b$:\n$$ J_{salt}(t"
      }, {
        "text": ") \u003d (\\Phi_m \\cdot t) \\cdot b^2 $$\n*Note: $\\Phi_m$"
      }, {
        "text": " is the mass flow rate (kg/s).*\n\n**Step 2: Angular Velocity as a function of time**\nUsing"
      }, {
        "text": " conservation $\\Gamma_0 \u003d J(t) \\omega(t)$:\n$$ \\omega(t) \u003d \\"
      }, {
        "text": "frac{\\Gamma_0}{J_{plate} + \\Phi_m b^2 t} $$\nThis can be simplified"
      }, {
        "text": " to the form:\n$$ \\omega(t) \u003d \\omega_0 \\frac{A}{B + t"
      }, {
        "text": "} $$\nWhere $A$ and $B$ represent the constant inertia terms.\n\n**Step 3: Calculating Angle"
      }, {
        "text": " of Rotation ($\\phi$)**\nTo find the total angle turned, we integrate angular velocity:\n$$ \\phi(t"
      }, {
        "text": ") \u003d \\int_0^t \\omega(t\u0027) dt\u0027 \u003d \\int_0^t \\frac{"
      }, {
        "text": "C}{D + t\u0027} dt\u0027 $$\n**Integration Recall:** $\\int \\frac{1}{x} dx \u003d \\ln|"
      }, {
        "text": "x|$.\n$$ \\phi(t) \u003d C \\left[ \\ln(D + t\u0027) \\right]_0^t"
      }, {
        "text": " \u003d C \\ln\\left(\\frac{D+t}{D}\\right) $$\n\n\u003e **Critical Analysis:** The lecturer emphasizes"
      }, {
        "text": " that while $\\omega$ decreases as mass is added (or changes), the total angle $\\phi$ grows logarithmically."
      }, {
        "text": " This is a classic \"rocket equation\" style integration but applied to rotation.\n\n---\n\n### 2.2. [[Inelastic Coll"
      }, {
        "text": "isions]]: Rod and Dart (Pikado)\n**Context:** A wooden rod of mass $m_{rod}$ and length $d$ hangs"
      }, {
        "text": " or pivots. A dart (pikado) of mass $m$ hits it with velocity $v$.\n\n#### Scenario"
      }, {
        "text": " A: Dart hits a hanging rod\n1.  **Conservation of Angular Momentum:** The linear momentum of the dart is converted"
      }, {
        "text": " into angular momentum of the system relative to the pivot.\n    $$ \\Gamma_{dart} \u003d \\vec{r} \\times \\"
      }, {
        "text": "vec{p} \u003d d \\cdot (m v) $$\n2.  **System Moment of Inertia ("
      }, {
        "text": "After Impact):**\n    $$ J_{total} \u003d J_{rod} + J_{dart} $$\n    *   "
      }, {
        "text": "$J_{rod}$ around pivot (using Steiner if pivot is at end): $J_{rod} \u003d \\frac{1}{3"
      }, {
        "text": "} m_{rod} d^2$.\n    *   $J_{dart} \u003d m_{dart} d^2$ (treated"
      }, {
        "text": " as point mass at distance $d$).\n3.  **Resulting Angular Velocity:**\n    $$ \\omega \u003d \\frac{\\Gamma_{dart"
      }, {
        "text": "}}{J_{total}} $$\n\n#### Scenario B: Energy Loss ($\\Delta W$)\nThe collision is plastic (inelastic). Energy is **"
      }, {
        "text": "not** conserved.\n$$ \\Delta W \u003d W_{final} - W_{initial} \u003d \\frac{1}{2} J"
      }, {
        "text": "_{total} \\omega^2 - \\frac{1}{2} m_{dart} v^2 $$\n"
      }, {
        "text": "\u003e **Warning:** A common student error is to try to conserve Energy during the impact. **Do not do this.** Only"
      }, {
        "text": " Angular Momentum is conserved during the impact forces. Energy is lost to deformation/heat.\n\n---\n\n### 2.3. [[Rotational"
      }, {
        "text": " Energy]]: The Acrobat/Skier\n**Context:** An acrobat or skier changes their body shape mid-flight (t"
      }, {
        "text": "ucking in arms/legs).\n*   **Initial state:** Large moment of inertia $J_1$, slow rotation $\\omega_1$.\n"
      }, {
        "text": "*   **Final state:** Small moment of inertia $J_2$, fast rotation $\\omega_2$.\n\n**"
      }, {
        "text": "Calculations:**\n1.  **Conservation:** $J_1 \\omega_1 \u003d J_2 \\omega_2 \\"
      }, {
        "text": "implies \\omega_2 \u003d \\omega_1 \\frac{J_1}{J_2}$.\n2."
      }, {
        "text": "  **Work Done by Acrobat:** The acrobat must perform work to pull their mass inward against centrifugal force. This manifests as an increase in kinetic"
      }, {
        "text": " energy.\n    $$ \\Delta W_{kin} \u003d \\frac{1}{2} J_2 \\omega_2^2 -"
      }, {
        "text": " \\frac{1}{2} J_1 \\omega_1^2 $$\n    Since $J_1 \u003e J_2"
      }, {
        "text": "$ and angular momentum is constant, $W_{kin}$ actually **increases**.\n\n---\n\n### 2.4. [[Dynamics"
      }, {
        "text": "]]: Block on an Inclined Plane\n**Context:** A block of mass $m\u003d50kg$ is pushed"
      }, {
        "text": "/pulled up a slope ($d\u003d6m$, $\\alpha\u003d30^\\circ$) with constant velocity. Friction"
      }, {
        "text": " coefficient $k_{tr}\u003d0.2$.\n\n**Objective:** Calculate the force $F$ required and the Work"
      }, {
        "text": " done ($A$).\n\n**Force Decomposition:**\nThe force $F$ acts at an angle $\\alpha$ relative to the slope"
      }, {
        "text": " (horizontal push on a wedge geometry).\n1.  **Axes:**\n    *   $x$: Parallel to slope"
      }, {
        "text": ".\n    *   $y$: Perpendicular to slope.\n2.  **Forces in $y$ (Per"
      }, {
        "text": "pendicular):**\n    $$ F_N - F_g \\cos\\alpha - F \\sin\\alpha \u003d 0 $$\n"
      }, {
        "text": "    $$ F_N \u003d mg \\cos\\alpha + F \\sin\\alpha $$\n    *Note: The pushing"
      }, {
        "text": " force $F$ adds to the normal force because it has a component pushing into the slope.*\n3.  **Forces in $x$ ("
      }, {
        "text": "Parallel, moving up):**\n    $$ F \\cos\\alpha - F_g \\sin\\alpha - F_{tr}"
      }, {
        "text": " \u003d 0 $$\n    Where Friction $F_{tr} \u003d k_{tr} F_N$.\n\n**Solving"
      }, {
        "text": " for F:**\nSubstitute $F_N$ into the $x$-equation:\n$$ F \\cos\\alpha - mg"
      }, {
        "text": " \\sin\\alpha - k_{tr}(mg \\cos\\alpha + F \\sin\\alpha) \u003d 0 $$\nGroup terms with $F"
      }, {
        "text": "$:\n$$ F (\\cos\\alpha - k_{tr} \\sin\\alpha) \u003d mg (\\sin\\alpha + k_{tr}"
      }, {
        "text": " \\cos\\alpha) $$\n$$ F \u003d mg \\frac{\\sin\\alpha + k_{tr} \\cos\\alpha"
      }, {
        "text": "}{\\cos\\alpha - k_{tr} \\sin\\alpha} $$\n\n**Calculating Work ($A$):**\n$$"
      }, {
        "text": " A \u003d \\int \\vec{F} \\cdot d\\vec{r} $$\nSince force is constant and parallel"
      }, {
        "text": " to displacement component:\n$$ A \u003d (F \\cos\\alpha) \\cdot d $$\n*(Alternatively, calculate"
      }, {
        "text": " total work done against gravity and friction).*\n\n\u003e **Critical Analysis:** The formula for $F$ reveals a singularity. If $\\cos\\alpha - k"
      }, {
        "text": "_{tr} \\sin\\alpha \u003d 0$, the force required becomes infinite. This corresponds to the condition of \"self-locking\""
      }, {
        "text": " where pushing harder just increases friction more than it helps move the block.\n\n---\n\n## 3. [[Work and Energy]]:"
      }, {
        "text": " Bungee/Spring Problem\n**Context:** Mass $m$ falls from height $h$, attached to a spring/"
      }, {
        "text": "rope with stiffness $k$. Find max extension $x$.\n\n**Conservation of Energy:**\n$$ W_{initial} \u003d W_{final} +"
      }, {
        "text": " W_{losses} $$\n1.  **Initial:** Potential Energy $W_p \u003d m g (h+"
      }, {
        "text": "x)$. (Assuming reference level at bottom).\n    *   *Correction in notes:* Often reference is at equilibrium or"
      }, {
        "text": " start. Let\u0027s look at the notes: $W_{kin} + W_p + W_{elas} \u003d const"
      }, {
        "text": "$.\n2.  **State 1 (Top):** $v\u003d0$, extension\u003d0. Energy \u003d $"
      }, {
        "text": "m g h$.\n3.  **State 2 (Bottom):** $v\u003d0$, extension\u003d$x$. Energy"
      }, {
        "text": " \u003d $\\frac{1}{2} k x^2$.\n4.  **Work by Friction/Drag ($W_{pr}$):**"
      }, {
        "text": " If friction is present, $m g h \u003d \\frac{1}{2} k x^2 + W_{pr}$."
      }, {
        "text": "\n\n**Equation:**\n$$ m g (h+d) - \\frac{1}{2} k d^2 \u003d "
      }, {
        "text": "0 $$\nThis forms a quadratic equation for $d$ (distance stretched).\n$$ d \u003d \\frac{-b"
      }, {
        "text": " \\pm \\sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} $$\n\n---\n\n## 4. Notable Memorial"
      }, {
        "text": "izations\n*   **The \"Pikado\" (Dart) example:** The lecturer uses a specific scenario of a dart hitting a rod to"
      }, {
        "text": " illustrate angular momentum conservation versus energy loss.\n*   **\"Graceful\" Derivation:** The instructor jokingly referred to the messy board"
      }, {
        "text": " derivation of the variable mass problem as \"graciozno\" (graceful/elegant) despite the complexity.\n*   **The"
      }, {
        "text": " Logarithm:** Special emphasis was placed on the fact that while rotational speed drops with mass addition, the total angle leads"
      }, {
        "text": " to a logarithmic term ($\\ln(t)$).\n\n---\n\n## 5. [[Warning]] / Common Pitfalls\n"
      }, {
        "text": "1.  **Steiner\u0027s Theorem:** Do not forget to shift the moment of inertia if the rotation axis is not"
      }, {
        "text": " the center of mass.\n    *   *Correct:* $J \u003d J_{cm} + md^2$.\n    *"
      }, {
        "text": "   *Incorrect:* $J \u003d J_{cm}$.\n2.  **Normal Force on Incline:** When an"
      }, {
        "text": " external force $F$ pushes on a block at an angle, $F_N$ is **not** just $mg \\cos\\alpha$. You"
      }, {
        "text": " must account for the component of $F$ pressing into the surface ($F \\sin\\alpha$). This increases friction.\n3.  **Conservation"
      }, {
        "text": " Confusion:**\n    *   **Collision:** Conserve **Momentum/Angular Momentum**. Energy is usually lost.\n    *   "
      }, {
        "text": "**Movement (Springs/Gravity):** Conserve **Energy**. Momentum changes due to external forces (gravity/spring mount"
      }, {
        "text": ")."
      }, {
